dedupe_keys.name: ed simulation netlogo agent based model of patient flow in an italian hospital emergency department moving to a new building

description: ED simulation is a small agent-based model of how a hospital emergency department works, written in NetLogo by Emilio Sulis and published in the CoMSES Computational Model Library in 2017. It was built for an Italian hospital that was moving its emergency department into a new building, so the simulations compare the old and new layouts. Activities such as registration, triage, visits and examinations are laid out as areas on the department map, and patients and staff (triage and ED nurses, doctors and support workers) move between them as agents. Each patient carries an urgency level (the white, green, yellow and red codes), which sets the path through the department. Version 1.0.0 is available as a free download from CoMSES under a CC-BY-4.0 licence. Caveats: the model is a single case with no documentation beyond the library page, the release notes are a placeholder, and no validation data are included. Coverage is one hospital in Italy, but the structure applies to other emergency departments. Simulation uses: testing layout and staffing changes, and adding patient flow to hospital disruption scenarios. Related records: the TraffGo PedGo model (model-traffgo-pedgo) covers movement of people in buildings at evacuation scale.
inputs: Emergency department floor plan with activity areas (registration, triage, visit, exams)
Patient arrivals by urgency (ESI colour codes) and staff numbers
name: ED simulation: NetLogo agent-based model of patient flow in an Italian hospital emergency department moving to a new building
outputs: Patient paths and waiting through the ED activities
Workload of nurses, doctors and support staff
